node.title: Re^2: Using constants as hash keys
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
it really doesn't have the notion of a "compile-time constant,"

I have to say this is incorrect. Perl has [doc://perlsub#Constant-Functions] and their effect is compile-time, note how print "foo" is optimized away completely  (edited slightly for brevity):

$ perl -MO=Deparse use constant DOFOO => 0; my $DOBAR = 0; print "foo" if DOFOO; print "bar" if $DOBAR; __END__ use constant ('DOFOO', 0); my $DOBAR = 0; '???'; print 'bar' if $DOBAR;
But, in so doing, they became misleading. You might well not actually know the implementation or the behavior of the language-constructs that you are looking at.

I find this misleading because it makes it sound like there is some undefined behavior here. Whether or not a function was inlined or not should be transparent to the user. And what [choroba] is writing about has more to do with the autoquoting happening on the LHS of the fat comma, which is also [doc://perlop#Comma-Operator|well defined] and has nothing to do with whether it's a constant function:

use Data::Dump; use constant FOO => 123; my $x = 455; sub BAR { ++$x } my %h = ( FOO => "A", BAR => "B", (FOO) => "C", (BAR) => "D", ); dd \%h; __END__ { 123 => "C", 456 => "D", BAR => "B", FOO => "A" }
The semantics were "grafted on,"

Constant functions have been around for something like 20 years, at least as far as I can tell from [https://perl5.git.perl.org/perl.git/blobdiff/b2a07c1c241ec86f010fc0ea3bfa54c8ec28be90..b88f04ff2985d0899964b90ae56789d88f6b353e:/pod/perlsub.pod|a quick look at the documentation]. I'm willing to concede a couple points: 1. constant, or rather readonly, variables aren't easily usable without somewhat obscure syntax (*PI=\3.14;, see [doc://perlmod#Symbol-Tables]) or a module like [mod://Readonly], 2. readonly variables don't have the same compile-time effect, and 3. constant functions require disambiguation when used as hash keys. However, taking the post as a whole, I'm sorry but IMO it is more FUD than fact.
